name: WebAssembly (WASM) inference
notable_features: WebAssembly enables near-native performance in browsers and standalone runtimes
WASM SIMD (128-bit SIMD) is critical for LLM inference - shipped in all major browsers
WASM threads enable multi-threaded inference via SharedArrayBuffer
llama.cpp WASM build runs GGUF models in the browser
ONNX Runtime Web runs ONNX models with WASM backend
Standalone WASM runtimes (Wasmtime, WasmEdge) enable server-side WASM inference
hardware_caveats: Performance is 2-10x slower than native CPU inference without SIMD
WASM SIMD is 128-bit vs 256-bit AVX2 - half the SIMD throughput
WASM threads require SharedArrayBuffer and cross-origin isolation
Memory is limited by WASM linear memory (4GB max in most runtimes)
No direct GPU access - WASM is CPU-only (WebGPU is the GPU path)
Smaller ecosystem than native inference - fewer optimized kernels
best_for: Cross-platform inference in browsers and standalone runtimes
Server-side inference with WASM sandboxing (Wasmtime, WasmEdge)
Applications requiring near-native performance without native compilation
Small to medium models (1-13B) with WASM SIMD
avoid_for: Maximum performance - native CPU/GPU inference is 2-10x faster
Large models (70B+) - WASM memory constraints are too tight
Production serving - no batching, scheduling, or multi-tenant support
notes: WebAssembly enables near-native CPU inference in browsers and standalone runtimes. WASM SIMD (128-bit) is critical for LLM inference performance. The primary use cases are llama.cpp WASM build (GGUF models in browser) and ONNX Runtime Web (ONNX models). WASM is CPU-only - WebGPU is the GPU path. Performance is 2-10x slower than native CPU inference.
